newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso still firm on smooth elections.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso still firm on smooth elections.

text.p: The Mexican peso had trimmed some of its initial sharp gains by late morning trade on Monday, but was still strong on a warm market reception of Sunday's smooth electoral process.

"I think the majority already knew the PRD would win (Mexico City)," a dealer said. "But I think the most important thing is the elections were clean." Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas won the Mexico City mayoralty.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were 4.3 and 4.4 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.9010/7.9040 and 7.8990/7.9010 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile closed trade for the day 3.4 centavos firmer at 7.8970/7.8990 per dollar.

Mexicans voted on Sunday for a new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City. Previously, that post had been filled by a presidential nominee.
Preliminary results showed President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) had lost overall control of the lower house for the first time since 1929.
Analysts stressed the relative lack of allegations of fraud, that have often marred elections in the past, were almost as important as the results themselves.
